title: Why Russell's band was exciting and never lost a battle at the Savoy
summary: Holmes argues Russell's band deserves more recognition, swung hard and won every Savoy band battle, though its records have a monotonous rhythm.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: To me that's one of the greatest bands ever...

Well, he had a band, believe me. And why he cannot get no recognition today, I don't know. I mean, they name everybody else's band, but you never hear nothin' about Russell's band. And Russell won every band they played against at the Savoy. He had never lost a battle in the Savoy against nobody. I'm not just saying that because I was in it. Not that they had the best-soundin' band in the world. But they sounded better in what they was playing than the other bands.

It was an exciting band. It sounded exciting anyway. I mean, musically speaking, they wasn't the best musical band, where everything was just so this-that-and-the-other. But they was an exciting band. They didn't have a whole lot of intricate arrangements with this-that-and-the-other, but they were swingin'.

In fact, I think that's what was wrong with the recordings was the same monotonous rhythm; they same rhythm all the time, you understand what I mean? Like, you'd hear that guitar and bass, and you'd hear that same steady rhythm all through the number. But that's what he wanted. He
wanted that rhythm. And what's what you needed when people are on the floor dancing. That's what they dance to, is the rhythm.
